Container.Name: MagicMirror
Container.Overview: MagicMirror² is an open source modular smart mirror platform. It turns a display behind a two-way mirror, a wall tablet or simply a browser tab into a personal dashboard showing clock, calendar, weather, news and hundreds of community modules.[br][br]This template runs MagicMirror² in server-only mode, the correct mode for a headless Unraid server: the interface is served over HTTP and rendered in any browser or on a separate client device such as a Raspberry Pi. The electron scenario, which draws to a locally attached display, will not work on Unraid and is deliberately not offered.[br][br][b]Two one-time steps are required, otherwise the container will not work.[/b][br][br][b]1. Fix the appdata permissions before the first start.[/b] The image runs as UID and GID 1000, but Unraid creates appdata as 99:100. Open the Unraid terminal and run:[br][br]mkdir -p /mnt/user/appdata/magicmirror/config /mnt/user/appdata/magicmirror/modules[br]chown -R 1000:1000 /mnt/user/appdata/magicmirror[br][br]Without this the container log shows "No write permission for /opt/magic_mirror/config" and no configuration is ever created.[br][br][b]2. Make the interface reachable on your network.[/b] On first start the container copies MagicMirror²'s stock config.js into the config folder. That stock configuration listens on localhost only and whitelists just the loopback address, so the WebUI will refuse your connection. Edit /mnt/user/appdata/magicmirror/config/config.js and set address to 0.0.0.0, then extend ipWhitelist with your own subnet, for example 192.168.0.0/16. Setting ipWhitelist to an empty list allows every address. Restart the container afterwards.[br][br]MagicMirror² has no built-in authentication. Keep it on a trusted network and do not expose the port directly to the internet. Use a VPN or an authenticated HTTPS reverse proxy for remote access.[br][br]The container image is built and maintained by Karsten Hassel at https://gitlab.com/khassel/magicmirror. This template provides only the Unraid packaging.

Container.Requires: Two one-time setup steps are required before the container is usable. The appdata directories must be owned by UID and GID 1000, and config.js must be changed to listen on 0.0.0.0 with your subnet added to ipWhitelist. Both are described in the overview and in the README. MagicMirror² is unauthenticated: keep it on a trusted LAN or behind a VPN or authenticated HTTPS reverse proxy.
Container.Changes: Initial release of the Unraid Community Applications template. Runs MagicMirror² in server-only mode from karsten13/magicmirror:debian-server, with selectable wolfi-server and alpine variants, persistent appdata for configuration and modules, and documented first-run permission and network binding steps.
Container.DefaultTagDescription: Debian 13 based, server-only mode. Recommended for Unraid and offering the broadest module compatibility.

Branch.TagDescription: Wolfi based, server-only mode. Smaller image with a reduced CVE surface.
Alpine based, server-only mode. Smallest image, but some modules with native dependencies may fail to build.

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: Host port used to open the MagicMirror² interface. It must match the port set in config.js. Keep this port limited to your trusted network and do not expose it directly to the internet.

Config.Name: Configuration
Config.Description: Persistent directory holding config.js and custom.css. It must be owned by UID and GID 1000 before the first start, otherwise the container cannot create its configuration. Include this directory in backups.

Config.Name: Modules
Config.Description: Persistent directory holding third party modules. It must be owned by UID and GID 1000 before the first start. Include this directory in backups.

Config.Name: Timezone
Config.Description: Timezone used for logs and displayed times, for example Europe/Berlin. If left empty the container falls back to UTC and logs a warning.

Config.Name: Run mode
Config.Description: Run mode of the container. Keep this at server on Unraid. The electron mode requires a locally attached display and will not work on a headless server.

Config.Name: Show mouse cursor
Config.Description: Set to true to show the mouse cursor in the interface. Useful when MagicMirror² is displayed on a touchscreen or wall tablet.
